newsitem.title: GERMANY: HOCHTIEF LOOKS ABROAD FOR 1997 GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: HOCHTIEF LOOKS ABROAD FOR 1997 GROWTH.

text.p: Hochtief AG, one of Germany's largest building companies. on Wednesday said it expected satisfactory profit this year after good foreign output offset a weak first half on the German market.
The company reported a 6.9 percent rise to 5.9 billion marks ($3.1 billion) in construction output in the six months to June 30, despite a 6.2 percent decline in domestic business.
Foreign output advanced nearly 27 percent in the period.

"Hochtief achieves half of its construction output on the German building market, which developed unsatisfactorily in the first half of the year, thus continuing last year's trend," the company said in its interim report.
"The cause of this is essentially weak domestic demand due to economic conditions."

However Hochtief said its margins would not be affected so strongly this year by restructuring measures and said continued good earnings from foreign business should lead to a satisfactory profit overall.
In 1996 the company reported net profit of 146 million marks on output of some 12 billion marks.

Incoming orders fell 30.2 percent to 5.92 billion marks in the six-month period, largely due to the absence this year of a the single large order for the Athens airport which boosted orders by more than two billion marks in the year-ago period.
Orders in hand were at 13.25 billion marks at end-June, 5.7 percent down on the year-ago period.
Staff numbers fell by 5.2 percent to 39,740, as domestic staffing was cut by more than one fifth to 16,877.
